articles.title: Governo vai cumprir objetivo principal da meta de controle de gastos, diz ministro da Fazenda | G1
articles.standfirst: O aumento de despesas agrava a situação das contas, que registram resultados negativos nos últimos 3 anos.
articles.summary: O aumento de despesas agrava a situação das contas, que registram resultados negativos nos últimos 3 anos.
articles.body:
O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou que o governo vai formalizar no Congresso Nacional o compromisso de cumprir o objetivo principal da meta de controle de gastos. Durante a campanha eleitoral, o presidente Lula anunciou uma série de medidas com novas despesas.

Um levantamento da Instituição Fiscal Independente mostra que pelo menos R$ 34 bilhões em despesas anunciadas pelo governo para o próximo ano não estão no projeto de Orçamento, enviado ao Congresso em agosto. Como o reajuste do Bolsa Família e o Desenrola 3.0 - programa de renegociação de dívidas em que o governo vai comprar dívidas de pessoas físicas; o PIX MEI, que prevê o repasse de R$ 5 mil a microempreendedores; e o Pé-de-Meia Universitário, proposta anunciada durante a campanha que prevê apoio financeiro a estudantes durante a graduação.

O aumento de despesas agrava a situação das contas, que registram resultados negativos nos últimos três anos. De janeiro a agosto de 2026, a conta também foi negativa: quase R$ 95 bilhões de déficit. E a dívida pública atingiu 82,9% do Produto Interno Bruto - maior nível em mais de cinco anos.

Sem controle dos gastos, o governo tem mais dificuldade para cumprir a meta fiscal, e o Banco Central não consegue baixar os juros. A meta de 2027 prevê um superávit - ou seja, as contas no azul - em 0,5% do PIB - cerca de R$ 73 bilhões. A regra permite variar esse resultado dentro de uma banda, um intervalo de tolerância.

Governo vai cumprir objetivo principal da meta de controle de gastos, diz ministro da Fazenda — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Sem dar prazo para o anúncio, o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, disse que o governo prepara medidas para buscar o centro da meta, o que, na prática, exige mais controle das despesas.

“Não vai acabar com a banda, mas nós vamos dizer e dar todos os instrumentos para que não haja dúvida jurídica de que a gente vai perseguir o centro da meta. Nós estamos agora passando por um período de transição e o governo, o presidente vai sentar tanto com a equipe atual quanto com a equipe que ele vai designar para o próximo mandato dele para que a gente defina os próximos passos concretos, sabendo que a gente já tem medidas aí prontas, como a busca do centro da meta, que vão ser tratadas com o Congresso Nacional em breve”, afirma Dario Durigan, ministro da Fazenda.

O governo tem recorrido à margem de tolerância - as bandas da meta - e à retirada de despesas do cálculo da meta para acomodar mais gastos e não para buscar um ajuste das contas. Economistas alertam que é urgente tomar ações concretas para frear o avanço de despesas. As obrigatórias, que incluem os benefícios da Previdência, por exemplo, não param de crescer.

“A pressão não é por promessas. A pressão é por ações. Então, o que se espera é que, nesse novo mandato do presidente Lula, haja de fato uma redução na velocidade com que as despesas obrigatórias têm crescido. Caso contrário, as despesas obrigatórias vão continuar a crescer de uma forma que vai comprimir qualquer capacidade de investimento público e ações do Estado em outras frentes também relevantes”, diz Sérgio Firpo, coordenador do Observatório da Qualidade do Gasto Público do Insper.

“O que precisa de fato, e seria possível, é apresentar um plano para mostrar que o governo consegue fazer a despesa crescer em um ritmo mais lento. E não adianta dizer que esse plano é cumprir o arcabouço fiscal. Porque o arcabouço fiscal claramente não está conseguindo fazer com que a despesa cresça em um ritmo tal que melhore o resultado primário e enderece essa questão fundamental, que é a sustentabilidade da dívida pública”, afirma Jeferson Bittencourt, chefe de Macroeconomia/ASA.

articles.title: Passado o período eleitoral, é esperado que fundamentos da economia voltem a direcionar decisões dos investidores | G1
articles.standfirst: Depois da disparada do dólar e da queda forte da Bolsa na segunda-feira (26), o mercado financeiro viveu, nesta terça-feira (27), um dia mais calmo.
articles.summary: Depois da disparada do dólar e da queda forte da Bolsa na segunda-feira (26), o mercado financeiro viveu, nesta terça-feira (27), um dia mais calmo.
articles.body:
Depois da disparada do dólar e da queda forte da Bolsa na segunda-feira (26), o mercado financeiro viveu, nesta terça-feira (27), um dia mais calmo.

É um leilão de títulos do Tesouro Direto. O barulho típico das mesas de operações indica que, depois da turbulência da véspera, o mercado voltou a respirar. A bolsa, que de manhã até subiu, acabou com baixa de 0,5%, depois de cair 13% na segunda-feira (26). O índice Ibovespa, agora, fica no mesmo nível de dois meses atrás. E, no mercado futuro, os juros para 2032 caíram depois da forte oscilação das últimas três semanas.

Passado o período eleitoral, é esperado que os fundamentos da economia voltem a direcionar a decisão dos investidores : a entrada e saída de capital influenciando o dólar, os balanços das empresas impactando as ações e a política fiscal orientando o rumo dos juros. E parece consenso entre os analistas que o mercado financeiro têm pressa de ver ações concretas do governo reeleito na direção dos desafios econômicos do país. A economista Andrea Ângelo diz que a prioridade é cuidar da escalada da dívida pública.

“O recado é celeridade. O governo precisa agir, esse novo governo reeleito, ele precisa agir com medidas concretas, sinais positivos para que o mercado mude. Não é humor que a gente está falando, mas mude a percepção mesmo de investimento, mude a percepção de política econômica que esse governo tende a fazer no próximo mandato”, afirma Andréa Angelo, economista da Warren Investimentos.

Passado o período eleitoral, é esperado que fundamentos da economia voltem a direcionar decisões dos investidores — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O dólar inverteu o movimento de segunda-feira (26), quando subiu mais de 8%. Nesta terça-feira (27), a moeda americana caiu quase 1% e fechou a R$ 5,35. O presidente do Banco Central, Gabriel Galípolo, disse que não deve entrar no mercado para mexer na cotação:

“O Banco Central sempre cumprindo sua função institucional, está ali para prestar todas as informações sobre os movimentos do mercado. Quando a gente vir, a gente vai atuar. A gente atua só em caso de disfuncionalidades, como a gente falou".

Não há motivos macroeconômicos que levem a esperar uma escalada do dólar, na opinião do economista André Perfeito.

“Qualquer relação de pares de moedas é sempre esse jogo de fluxo. O fluxo financeiro, ou seja, a taxa de juros está atrativa aqui no Brasil, porque subiu bastante já, e a balança comercial está positiva. Então, cabe à autoridade monetária só observar se o pânico não vai desorganizar demais. A gente está vendo que o mercado, ao voltar ao que estava antes do primeiro turno, está querendo agora tatear, entender o que de fato o governo eleito vai oferecer, que tipo de ajuste fiscal ele pretende fazer, como ele pretende endereçar algumas questões”, diz André Perfeito, economista-chefe da Garantia Capital.

articles.title: FMI fecha acordo com a Argentina e pode liberar mais US$ 900 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Valor faz parte do acordo de US$ 20 bilhões firmado entre a Argentina e a instituição em 2025. O repasse, no entanto, ainda depende da aprovação do conselho executivo da instituição.
articles.summary: Valor faz parte do acordo de US$ 20 bilhões firmado entre a Argentina e o fundo em 2025. O repasse, no entanto, ainda depende da aprovação do conselho executivo da instituição.
articles.body:
O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, em 2 de abril de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Agustin Marcarian

O Fundo Monetário Internacional ( FMI ) e a Argentina chegaram nesta terça-feira (27) a um acordo que pode liberar cerca de US$ 900 milhões ao país (R$ 4,8 bilhões). O repasse, no entanto, ainda depende da aprovação do conselho executivo da instituição.

O valor faz parte do programa de financiamento de US$ 20 bilhões firmado entre a Argentina e o FMI em 2025 . A liberação dos US$ 900 milhões está ligada à terceira revisão do programa, em que o fundo verifica o cumprimento das metas acertadas com o país.

Na avaliação do FMI, a economia argentina apresentou avanços desde a última análise. A instituição destacou a continuidade da desaceleração da inflação e o aumento das reservas internacionais, que ficaram acima do previsto no programa.

🔎 Na prática, os recursos ajudam a reforçar as reservas internacionais da Argentina. Esse estoque de dólares é importante para o país pagar compromissos no exterior e dá mais fôlego ao governo de Javier Milei para flexibilizar as restrições ao uso da moeda americana.

Desde o início do programa de US$ 20 bilhões , o FMI já desembolsou cerca de US$ 15,8 bilhões à Argentina. Se a nova parcela for aprovada, outros US$ 900 milhões ficarão disponíveis ao país. Relembre os repasses:

Abril de 2025: US$ 12 bilhões , liberados na aprovação do programa.

Julho de 2025: cerca de US$ 2 bilhões , após a primeira revisão.

Maio de 2026: cerca de US$ 1 bilhão , após a aprovação da segunda revisão. À época, o FMI informou que, com o desembolso, o total acumulado chegou a cerca de US$ 15,8 bilhões.

Outubro de 2026: cerca de US$ 900 milhões, ainda sujeitos à aprovação.

O que o FMI diz sobre a economia argentina

Um dos principais avanços apontados pelo FMI está nas reservas internacionais da Argentina, uma espécie de colchão de dólares do país.

No comunicado divulgado nesta terça-feira, a instituição destacou que as reservas líquidas superaram a meta estabelecida no programa.

“Como resultado, as reservas internacionais líquidas superaram em cerca de US$ 4 bilhões a meta para o fim de junho, e o Banco Central comprou quase US$ 16 bilhões até agora neste ano", afirmou o FMI.

A recomposição das reservas é uma das frentes acompanhadas pela instituição dentro do programa de financiamento.

O ajuste também passa pelas contas públicas. Na área fiscal, o governo argentino deverá buscar um superávit primário de 1,4% do PIB em 2026 e manter esforço semelhante em 2027 , destacou o FMI. Na prática, significa arrecadar mais do que gastar, sem considerar os juros da dívida.

Para os próximos meses, a instituição afirma que a Argentina deverá continuar reforçando suas reservas e buscando fontes de financiamento. O FMI acrescentou ainda que as autoridades se comprometeram a preparar o país para voltar ao mercado internacional.

articles.title: El Niño pode provocar perdas de R$ 33 bilhões na safra de soja do Brasil; entenda os riscos | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo estima que um El Niño forte pode reduzir a produção brasileira em quase 18 milhões de toneladas. MT e GOconcentrariam as maiores perdas, enquanto o RS poderia se beneficiar das chuvas.
articles.summary: Estudo estima que um El Niño forte pode reduzir a produção brasileira em quase 18 milhões de toneladas. MT e GOconcentrariam as maiores perdas, enquanto o RS poderia se beneficiar das chuvas.
articles.body:
Produção de soja é marcada por expectativas e desafios em 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Aprosoja

A safra brasileira de soja 2026/27 pode ter uma queda de cerca de 10% caso o El Niño seja forte, reduzindo a produção de 181,2 milhões para 163,6 milhões de toneladas.

A estimativa faz parte de um estudo divulgado nesta terça-feira (27) pela Serasa Experian, que analisou os possíveis impactos do fenômeno climático nas principais regiões produtoras do país.

O Brasil é o maior produtor e exportador mundial de soja. Segundo o estudo, a projeção considera uma expansão de 900 mil hectares na área plantada , alta de 1,8% em relação à safra anterior, chegando a 49,9 milhões de hectares .

Mesmo com a expansão da área plantada, porém, a falta de chuva e as temperaturas elevadas poderiam reduzir a produtividade das lavouras.

As maiores perdas se concentrariam no Centro-Oeste. Segundo a Serasa, Mato Grosso poderia perder 9,7 milhões de toneladas de soja , enquanto Goiás teria uma redução de 4 milhões de toneladas na produção.

O levantamento foi divulgado enquanto o plantio da safra avança rapidamente em várias regiões do país. No Sul, porém, o excesso de chuva tem dificultado os trabalhos no campo.

Dados divulgados nesta segunda-feira (26) pela AgRural mostram que 40% da área prevista para o cultivo de soja no Brasil já havia sido plantada até quinta-feira (22).

Risco climático vai do plantio ao desenvolvimento da lavoura

Segundo Daniel de Oliveira, gerente de geoprocessamento agro da Serasa Experian, os riscos associados ao El Niño entram em uma nova fase. A preocupação deixa de se concentrar apenas nas condições para o plantio e passa a envolver também a distribuição das chuvas durante o desenvolvimento das lavouras.

"Quando começa a olhar para regiões relevantes, o risco deixa de ser para a implantação, mas como as chuvas vão ser distribuídas... para que o produtor não enfrente redução da produtividade tal como vimos na 2023/24", disse ele.

Oliveira afirmou que os produtores aproveitaram a segunda quinzena de outubro para acelerar o plantio, fazendo com que o ritmo dos trabalhos voltasse à "normalidade" em Mato Grosso.

"Mas o risco ainda não desapareceu, ainda não conseguimos dizer que a safra 26/27 está livre dos impactos que a gente está discutindo nesse estudo", afirmou.

Segundo ele, as condições climáticas ainda precisarão ser favoráveis ao florescimento das plantas e à formação dos grãos, etapas que ocorrerão em novembro e dezembro em importantes estados produtores.

Na última ocorrência de El Niño forte, em 2024, a produtividade média da soja brasileira caiu mais de 8%, para 3.282 quilos por hectare, na comparação com 2023, quando houve um episódio fraco de La Niña. Os dados são da Companhia Nacional de Abastecimento (Conab).

Se a produtividade cair conforme o cenário projetado, as perdas para o setor podem chegar a R$ 33 bilhões, segundo a Serasa. A estimativa considera os preços de agosto.

A empresa ressalta, porém, que a redução da oferta de soja tende a elevar os preços do grão, o que pode mudar as condições de venda e o impacto financeiro para os produtores.

Os efeitos do El Niño seriam diferentes entre as regiões do país. No Rio Grande do Sul, a produção poderia crescer 5,5 milhões de toneladas, já que o estado costuma registrar mais chuvas durante episódios do fenômeno.

No pior cenário projetado pela Serasa, 13 estados brasileiros registrariam queda de produtividade, enquanto outros quatro poderiam ter pequenos ganhos.

Além de Mato Grosso e Goiás, a projeção aponta queda de produtividade no Paraná, em São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Mato Grosso do Sul, Bahia e Maranhão, entre outros estados.

articles.title: Gold prices have plunged: Should you buy yellow metal this Diwali?
articles.summary: By Vedika Narvekar Every Diwali, Indian investors ask us one question: Is it the right time to buy gold? And our answer? Absolutely!
articles.body: By Vedika NarvekarEvery Diwali, Indian investors ask us one question: Is it the right time to buy gold? And our answer? Absolutely! However, this year, the answer isn’t so simple. Gold has fallen more than 26% from its January record high, yet in rupee terms, it is still 11.6% higher than last Diwali.There is considerable uncertainty in global markets, which would normally boost gold’s safe-haven appeal. However, the yellow metal is currently responding more to elevated bond yields and interest rate expectations.Meanwhile, in India, mutual funds have closed one door, jewellers are reporting strong sales, and global investors have started buying again. So, let’s understand what’s driving the gold market and whether this Diwali presents the right opportunity to invest.The Diwali-to-Diwali scorecardIf we look at gold from one Diwali to the next and it has rewarded patient buyers. On the MCX, gold has risen from Rs 50,986 per 10 gm in November 2020 to about Rs 1,45,800 now. That is almost 3 times the price.It has fallen in only one of the seven Diwali-to-Diwali periods (down 6.7% in 2021). The best run was last year, when it jumped 66.5%.International gold (Comex) tells a quieter story. It has gone from $1,888 to about $4,110 per ounce, but it is down 5.7% this year, and it also fell in 2021 and 2022.Why is gold down in dollars but up in rupees? Because of the weaker rupee and the import duty hike in May, from 6% to 15%. Both have cushioned Indian buyers from the global fall.Lets understand why gold fell globally Higher rates and a stronger dollar did most of the damage. The US 10-year yield is above 5%, its highest since 2002, and the dollar index is near 102, close to an 18-month high. Gold fell 8.5% in September to $4,176 as the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points, its first hike since 2023, and a December hike is priced at about 90%. US inflation is 3.7%, and Brent is up over 75% this year to about $108 since the US-Iran war began in late February.Buyer support has also weakened. China's central bank bought 23t in September and 103t this year, and central banks bought 170t in January-August. But Russia sold 56t, Turkey net sold 82t, and Kazakhstan plans to cut gold to 75% of reserves from 78%.Physical demand is soft too: China's wholesale demand fell 21% y/y to 234t in July-September, and India's gold imports were $1.8 billion in September, down 81% y/y.What buyers are doingGlobal ETFs are back. After dipping in the April-July period, following the war's outbreak, global gold ETF demand has risen steadily: $18 billion in August, $10 billion (67.3t) in September, and a record $31 billion for the July-September quarter. Total holdings are at a record 4,256t, and North American funds had their first quarterly inflow of 2026.India's ETFs follow the trend. Indian gold ETFs took in Rs 4,450 crore in September, a seven-month high, adding about 3t to reach 124t. Another Rs 1,722 crore came in the first half of October. About 140,000 new accounts were opened in September, against around 4,000 in August. Digital gold also rose, with 1.7t bought in September, 83% more by value than a year ago.Jewellery is resilient, coins are cooling. Listed jewellers grew revenue 20-30% in July-September even though key festivals fall in the next quarter this year, and same-store sales rose about 20%. Buyers are choosing lighter pieces, average bills are up by double digits, and old-gold exchange makes up over half of sales at some retailers.Coin and bar demand, however, has cooled from a strong base as price momentum eased. The discount on domestic gold has narrowed from $66 an ounce in September to $8, a sign that festive demand is returning.Different avenues and their pros and consGold can be bought through jewellery, coins and bars, Gold ETFs, gold FoFs, digital gold and MCX gold derivatives. Jewellery suits wearing and gifting but involves making charges and GST, while coins and bars have lower making charges but require safe storage. Gold ETFs offer exchange-traded exposure without storage concerns but require a demat account.Gold FoFs allow easy SIPs without a demat account, though fresh investments may be restricted by some fund houses. Digital gold starts at Rs 1 but carries 3% GST, a 2.5-5% buy-sell spread and lacks SEBI regulation.MCX gold derivatives allow investors to gain exposure to gold price movements with relatively low upfront margin and no physical storage, but involve leverage, high volatility, margin calls and the risk of substantial losses. The simple rule is buy jewellery to wear and ETFs for long-term investment and allocate 10-12% of a portfolio to gold.The outlook until next DiwaliThe next trigger is the US Fed meeting on 27-28 October. Markets see about an 82% chance of no change, but a December hike is largely priced in. In the short term (1 month), we expect Spot gold to stay in the range of $3,950-4,320 and on the MCX Rs 1,39,500- Rs 1,53,000. Beyond that, there are three scenarios:• Cautious: The Fed keeps tightening and oil stays high. In such a scenario, Spot Gold could dip below $3,900 towards $3,800 level, which is about Rs 1,34,500 per 10 gm on the MCX.• Base case: Gold moves sideways, then recovers as festive and wedding demand, ETF flows and central bank buying offset higher rates. That is about $4,000-4,550, or Rs 1,41,000-1,61,000.• Positive: The hiking cycle ends and fears of currency debasement return. In such cases, Gold may rebound sharply towards $4,800-$4,850, or about Rs 1.72 lakh.Overall, any major geopolitical escalation, a surge in oil prices, or further Fed tightening could trigger a decline in MCX gold prices towards Rs 1,40,000 and below. However, in the absence of such developments, prices may consolidate around current levels of Rs 1,44,500-Rs 1,54,000, with limited downside.For prices to move beyond this range, the interest rate-hiking cycle would need to come to an end, potentially paving the way for a strong upside in MCX gold prices towards Rs 1,60,000-Rs 1,70,000. Considering these scenarios, the smart approach is to wait for a dip and buy gold in installments rather than all at once. Use ETFs for investment, and keep gold to around 10-12% of your portfolio. Avoid borrowing to buy gold.While gold may have lost some of its shine this year, it continues to hold a special place in Indian homes. This Diwali, the key is to buy wisely, plan ahead and invest within your means.(The author is Research Analyst - Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Shares and Stock Broker)(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Over 40% of Americans don't know how much they'll need for retirement
articles.summary: A new report shows that 40% of Americans don't know how much they need to retire. Here's why you shouldn't leave your retirement savings to chance and how to...
articles.body:

For many workers, retirement can feel so far away that months or even years pass without reviewing their plan or creating one at all.

In fact, many Americans do not know how much they'll need to support themselves in retirement. More than 4 in 10 Americans have never tried to calculate what retirement will cost them, according to a national survey of U.S. adults aged 25 to 75 from Evergreen.ai, a financial-planning platform.

Among those who expect to retire within 15 years, 1 in 3 still haven't run the numbers.

Why workers put retirement planning on the back burner

There are several reasons Americans may be putting off retirement planning.

The Employee Benefit Research Institute's 2026 Retirement Confidence Survey found that workers face several challenges, including concerns about changes to the retirement system, difficulty saving for retirement due to high healthcare and housing costs, uncertainty about where to turn for financial guidance, and mounting debt.

About 3 in 5 workers said debt negatively affects their ability to save for retirement.

"First, they don't even know where to start — there is so much information out there that it's overwhelming to start planning for retirement. People approaching retirement get information overload," said Nathan Nicolaisen, a certified financial planner and the founder of Redspire Wealth Management. "Second, they might be scared to look at their finances, so they avoid it. Third, they might feel like they don't need to plan and are in a good spot or that everything will work itself out."

The problem with hoping that things will just work themselves out without a clear plan is that you could end up falling behind without even realizing it — particularly if you miscalculate how much money you'll need to live comfortably in retirement.

Even people with a clear savings target will likely need to adjust that figure throughout their lives as their needs and income evolve. Certain living expenses, such as housing, may decrease as you age and downsize or pay off your mortgage, while others, such as healthcare, may increase as you get older.

You may also need to adjust your contributions if you aim to retire earlier or later than originally planned. Inflation, which erodes your money's purchasing power, matters too.

Many experts agree that failing to make a plan or failing to start saving as soon as possible, because you haven't figured out how much you need, could end up being a costly mistake in the long run.

"Most of the people I've met who are behind on retirement got there the same way. They assumed there was always more time," said Jay Pinkston, CFP®, founder of Pinkston Wealth. "Then one day they realize retirement is close, and now they're almost afraid to sit down and plan because they don't want to see how far behind they are."

Pinkston says the highest cost of waiting is lost compounding. "When I run retirement projections, an extra year of time often makes a bigger difference than saving more each month," he said.

Calculating your retirement number and building a savings plan

Northwestern Mutual's 2026 Planning & Progress Study found that Americans believe they'll need an average of $1.46 million to "retire comfortably," up from $1.25 million in 2022.

If that figure sounds out of your reach, you're not alone. The same study found that nearly a quarter of those with retirement savings report having just one year or less of their current annual income set aside for it.

The good news is that a smaller balance doesn't necessarily mean you're behind.

One common rule for determining your savings goal is to aim for 10 to 12 times your annual salary by retirement. This type of guideline could be a good starting point as you begin to create a plan, but your actual retirement savings goal should be more unique to your future lifestyle and expenses.

"I start with spending," said Pinkston. "Once we know what retirement will actually cost, we look at savings and retirement income to see whether it will last, and then we figure out what adjustments to make."

Some workers who have put off calculating their retirement costs because they're overwhelmed may find they aren't that far off track. Especially once they've factored in other sources of income, such as their Social Security benefits, annuities, spousal income, and other assets that could be used to cover costs.

In cases where someone finds that they're still quite a ways off from their desired target, experts say this doesn't mean the situation is hopeless. Savers can still take steps to boost their retirement savings by increasing their income and reducing current expenses and debt balances to make larger contributions.

This is also an opportunity to reevaluate not just how much you're saving, but where that money is being kept, and whether it's worth exploring alternative savings vehicles to maximize your money's growth potential.

"They have to start, and starting means taking an honest look at where they stand today before looking forward. Think of it like a map. You can't get directions to point B if you don't know where point A is," said Pinkston. "Once you know your starting point, the path forward gets a lot clearer, even if it's not the path you originally hoped for."

How much do you really need to save for retirement?

Figuring out how much you need to save for retirement can be tough, especially if it's still a long way off. These guidelines can help you determine the right amount.

Are you saving enough for retirement? Here's how to tell.

Do you need to be a millionaire to retire? Experts weigh in on the 15% rule.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) said Tuesday it will invest $1 billion in Meta Platforms' (META) equity offering as the chipmaker deepens its partnership with the Facebook parent to support its growing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure needs.

AMD also announced that its Helios computing systems are running at Meta, while its EPYC processors power Meta's Muse AI agent. The chipmaker said its technology also supports Meta's Muse Spark Open and Muse Glimmer models.

articles.title: Consumer sentiment increased in October: Conference Board
articles.summary: Consumer sentiment rose in October, as Americans’ views of present and future business conditions improved, according to a new survey. The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose from 84.2 in September to 91.7 this month. Last month’s index, which the Conference Board revised upward from 81.9, marked the metric’s lowest point in more than a…
articles.body:
Consumer sentiment rose in October, as Americans’ views of present and future business conditions improved, according to a new survey.

The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose from 84.2 in September to 91.7 this month. Last month’s index, which the Conference Board revised upward from 81.9, marked the metric’s lowest point in more than a decade.

The expectations index, based on consumers’ six-month outlook of economic conditions, increased by 6.9 points to 72.6. The index had declined for three consecutive months.

Fergus McCormick, a senior economist at the Conference Board, said consumer sentiment rising in October “was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September.”

A gallon of regular gas costs roughly $4.26 on average as of Tuesday, down about 22 cents from a month ago, according to AAA . Gas prices have risen throughout the Iran war , as the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz hamper the energy industry.

Diesel prices are also down by roughly 12 cents per gallon over the last month, AAA reported. A gallon of diesel fuel, however, is nearly $2.70 more expensive than a year ago.

Despite October’s uptick, consumer confidence “remained on the long-term downward trend that’s persisted over the past few years,” McCormick noted.

“Consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods over the next six months,” he added. “This likely reflected higher price levels and persistent inflation, which eroded consumers’ purchasing power.”

Annual inflation was 3.7 percent in September , up from 3.4 percent in August , according to the consumer price index . Energy prices also experienced their largest monthly increase since March, the first full month of the Iran conflict.

Americans’ view of the economy will define the midterms , as Republicans face headwinds and Democrats seek to snag control of Congress for the bulk of President Trump’s final two years in office.

articles.title: JetBlue stock rises despite Q3 loss, as demand remains 'resilient'
articles.summary: JetBlue (JBLU) reported a wider-than-expected third-quarter loss on Monday and cut its full-year margin outlook, but the stock jumped as demand remained stro...
articles.body:
JetBlue ( JBLU ) reported a wider-than-expected third quarter loss on Monday and cut its full-year margin outlook, but the stock jumped as demand remained strong.

JetBlue's adjusted loss per share was $0.60, versus the $0.55 expected by analysts, per Bloomberg consensus. Revenue rose 21.1% year over year to $2.81 billion.

The airline now expects a negative adjusted operating margin of 4.5% to 6.5% for 2026. That's worse than its previous forecast of negative 2% to 5%, and the midpoint of negative 5.8% missed analysts' expectations.

But JetBlue stock still rose over 19% on Tuesday after the airline said demand remains strong and has carried into the fourth quarter.

"Resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue well ahead of our initial expectations, allowing us to recapture more of the increase in fuel costs than we initially expected," CEO Joanna Geraghty said in a statement. "That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, and Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver exceptional results even as we significantly grow capacity."

Unit revenue (revenue per available seat mile, or what the airline earns for flying one seat one mile) rose 18.4%. Unit costs excluding fuel rose 7%.

Meanwhile, JetBlue paid an average of $3.91 a gallon, up 57.4%, which pushed fuel expense up 61% to $868 million. It expects to pay $4.64 a gallon in the fourth quarter.

The results arrive as bondholders grow nervous. Senior creditors are working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners and law firm Akin, the Wall Street Journal reported .

Creditors who hire advisers are usually organizing ahead of possible talks with the borrower, but it doesn't necessarily mean a restructuring is underway.

Much of JetBlue's debt is secured by its aircraft and its TrueBlue loyalty program. Total debt stood at $8.39 billion at the end of September, and the airline expects about $590 million in interest expense this year.

JetBlue ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity, including a $600 million undrawn credit facility. It expects $250 million in aircraft-backed financing to be funded in the fourth quarter, and it has about $7 billion in assets that aren't pledged as collateral.

"We believe we have the liquidity and financing options to create a strong bridge to at least $1 EPS," CFO Ursula Hurley said.

Recall that Spirit Airlines shut down this year following repeated bankruptcy filings; the company was poised to merge with JetBlue, but a federal court sided with the Biden administration in blocking the merger.

articles.title: US Offers Constellation $5 Billion Financing to Spur Nuclear
articles.summary: The Trump administration is offering as much as $5 billion in financing to Constellation Energy Corp. to upgrade and modernize the nuclear operator’s fleet o...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The Trump administration is offering as much as $5 billion in financing to Constellation Energy Corp. to upgrade and modernize the nuclear operator's fleet of reactors in Illinois, Maryland, and Pennsylvania.

The projects backed by the conditional loan commitment are expected to add nearly 1.1 gigawatts of electricity and help strengthen the grid and lower costs, according to the Energy Department. Constellation shares surged on the news.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright plans to announce the funding later Tuesday at an Illinois nuclear plant that will supply power to Alphabet Inc.'s Google.

"The Energy Department is accelerating President Trump's American nuclear renaissance and unlocking the full potential of our nation's nuclear fleet," Wright said in a statement. He said upgrades that increase output from existing nuclear facilities can expand electricity supply while supporting grid reliability and affordability for consumers and businesses.

Technology companies are driving interest in nuclear projects to power artificial intelligence. But new reactors can take a decade or more to permit and build. Upgrading components such as turbines can increase the output from existing plants, and is seen as a faster and cheaper way to deliver carbon-free fission electricity.

Constellation shares gained as much as 5.3%, and were up 2.8% to $259.63 at 11:39 a.m. in New York.

The Energy Department financing is part of President Donald Trump's push to expand nuclear power to meet growing electricity demand from data centers and support domestic manufacturing. The funding follows an executive order that set a goal of adding 5 gigawatts of capacity through upgrades at existing nuclear plants, 96% of which has been achieved, the department said.

Constellation is planning investments at six Illinois plants — Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities — as well as Calvert Cliffs in Maryland and Limerick in Pennsylvania to increase output from existing nuclear plants, the Energy Department said. The financing, through the department's Office of Energy Dominance Financing, also includes an option to fund future uprates at other Constellation facilities.

articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, y las oportunidades inmobiliarias: "Hay que detectar a Messi con 15 años y evitar comprarlo cuando tenga 30"
articles.standfirst: El economista analiza una de sus operaciones en el mercado de la vivienda
articles.summary: El economista analiza una de sus operaciones en el mercado de la vivienda
articles.body: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, ha informado a sus seguidores en las redes sociales de sus últimas operaciones inmobiliarias. "Hace dos años compré dos pisos en construcción en Zaragoza para destinar al alquiler en Arcosur. Muchos zaragozanos me criticaron la elección porque las ventas en dicha zona habían ido muy mal en el pasado", ha reflexionado en su cuenta personal de X. El profesor universitario ha indicado que el precio de estas viviendas ha subido un 30 por ciento en los últimos dos años. Acto seguido, Gonzalo Bernardos ha aconsejado a sus seguidores cuál debe ser su planteamiento a la hora de adquirir una propiedad: "La mayoría de los inversores en vivienda compran en la zona donde vive o en el centro de su ciudad. Hay que diversificar, mirar otras urbes y encontrar la oportunidad". El economista ha tirado de un símil futbolístico. "Para ello, hay que detectar a Messi con 15 años (eso es Arcosur) y evitar comprarlo cuando tenga 30 años", ha comentado. Adquirir a Leo Messi en etapa formativa era mucho más asequible que una vez se consagró en la élite mundial del fútbol, donde entonces su precio de mercado ya estaba por las nubes. El economista, en una publicación anterior, defendió el papel de los inversores en vivienda. "Si no hubiera inversión por parte de las familias en viviendas de alquiler, ¿qué hacemos con los que desean vivir de alquiler y no pueden comprar una vivienda? ¿Les proporcionamos una tienda de campaña?", preguntó. Gonzalo Bernardos argumentó entonces que tener viviendas en propiedad formaba parte de la economía de muchas familias: "Muchos españoles, que precisamente no son ricos, pero sí ahorradores que no quieren invertir en los mercados financieros, lo hacen en viviendas y las ponen en alquiler. Sin ellos, no habría inquilinos, pues la Administración sólo tiene 318.000 viviendas".

articles.title: Microsoft’s VEO: India employees face a tough stay-or-leave call
articles.summary: Microsoft offers voluntary exit option (VEO) to eligible India staff and others; decision due Dec 1 with severance, benefits and career support amid job-market worries.
articles.body: Bengaluru: When Microsoft rolled out its voluntary exit option (VEO), it surprised India-based employees who received the email, even if workforce changes were not entirely unexpected. For Gandhi, a software engineer at the company who chose to be identified this way, the immediate reaction was anxiety about what the future might hold.“It is quite scary, to be honest, because we don’t know where the future is heading and what will happen,” she told TOI.Gandhi said the option had been extended to eligible employees across participating organisations. But deciding whether to take the offer is not straightforward, particularly in a difficult job market. Employees have time to consider their options, and Gandhi said she was still trying to make sense of the situation.“Everything is so hazy right now. We can’t determine everything at this moment because they have given us time. So, we’ll think about it, get to know what is happening, and see how things unfold. It’s a very tight market,” she said.The prospect of switching jobs adds to the uncertainty. “Even switching jobs is a big thing. I have seen my friends trying to switch, but it’s very difficult,” she added.Microsoft is learnt to have offered the VEO to 60,000 employees across eligible organisations. Microsoft’s VEO covers AI Experiences, Copilot, Agents & Platform, CoreAI, Finance, Human Resources, the Office of the CTO, Strategy & Transformation, Windows + Devices, and Xbox. Cloud + AI, Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs (CELA), and Microsoft AI (MAI) are partially participating; employee eligibility varies, and leaders are expected to share further details by team. Marketing, Microsoft Commercial Business, Microsoft Discovery & Quantum, and Microsoft Security are not participating in the programme.Ironically, a day before Microsoft announced its voluntary exit option (VEO), co-founder Bill Gates was quoted in an interview published in The Observer on Sunday as saying: “The incentive structure is wrong. It’s ‘hire the robot, fire the human and don’t look back’.”The company has about 23,000 employees in India, though the number who received the offer in the country could not be independently ascertained.The programme is available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the UK and the US at level 70 and below. It is a time-limited, voluntary offer that allows employees to leave Microsoft with financial support and career-planning resources. Employees opting for the VEO must decide by Dec 1. The payout includes one month’s base salary for every completed year of service, health insurance and career-transition services.“There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee. These are a few of the ways we’re trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute,” said Amy Coleman, executive vice-president and chief people officer at Microsoft, in a blog post on Tuesday.Level 70 corresponds to the vice-president or partner-level/senior director tier. When contacted by TOI, Microsoft said, “India continues to be an important place for Microsoft’s business and talent to grow. VEO is a voluntary, time-limited offer for eligible employees who are thinking about their next chapter. For most eligible employees, now won’t be the right time to consider what’s next outside of Microsoft, but we are giving them that option. Future workforce needs will continue to be based on business needs and priorities. VEO is one option within a flexible set of workforce approaches.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Microsoft to report Q1 earnings with Wall Street looking for further Azure growth
articles.summary: Microsoft will report its Q1 earnings after the bell Wednesday.
articles.body:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) will report its first quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, providing the market with a better view of demand for AI apps and services.

The announcement comes just two days after Microsoft said it is offering buyouts to upward of 60,000 eligible employees as it seeks to reduce expenses amid its massive AI build-out.

Q1 also marks the first time Microsoft will report earnings under its new segment structure . The company announced the change in Q4, saying that rather than Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, it will switch to two segments: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.

Microsoft's Agents and Infra segment will garner the most attention and include the company's Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud services, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, and frontier and support services.

Devices and Consumer will include Microsoft's search and advertising businesses, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices.

Microsoft's stock was a laggard for most of fiscal 2026 but picked up following the company's Q4 earnings, climbing about 35% since July.

Investors following the company's Q1 report will be on the lookout for more information about Azure and Copilot growth as Microsoft continues to push its AI services.

For the quarter, Wall Street is anticipating earnings per share of $4.27 on revenue of $90.6 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. That would be an improvement from the EPS of $4.13 and revenue of $77.6 billion the company saw in the same period last year.

Agents and Infra revenue is expected to climb 22.5% to $75.6 billion, with Azure and Microsoft 365 bringing in $32.2 billion and $27.4 billion, respectively.

Devices and Consumer sales are projected to decline 6% to $15 billion.

Capital expenditures, including leases, are anticipated to top $45.9 billion in the quarter, up from the $19.3 billion Microsoft spent in Q1 last year.

Remaining performance obligations (RPO) are expected to come in at $705.6 billion, up 77% from the $389 billion reported in fiscal Q1 2026.

RPOs are contracts that Microsoft has booked with customers but hasn't yet received revenue for.

articles.body: Bengaluru: AI infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million led by Dallas Venture Capital, with Nvidia among the investors, to expand its software that helps businesses run AI applications more efficiently.Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax also participated in the round. The company did not disclose its valuation following the funding. The proceeds will support product development, cloud partnerships and expansion across North America and other markets.TOI first reported on April 11 that NVentures, Nvidia’s venture capital arm, was investing in Simplismart as part of the funding round.Simplismart focuses on inference, the process through which a trained AI model responds to a request, such as generating a video or answering a question. Its software helps companies manage the speed, cost and reliability of AI models across cloud services and their own infrastructure.“The advantage comes from how you run them: what each interaction costs, how quickly the application responds, and whether it stays reliable as demand grows,” said Amritanshu Jain, co-founder and CEO.The company said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14-fold over six months, without disclosing the revenue figure. A run rate projects annual revenue based on performance over a shorter period. Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema.Simplismart cited customer communications platform Exotel as an example of potential savings. Exotel adapted an open-source model using its own data and moved it to Simplismart after finding proprietary-model services too expensive, according to the announcement.Simplismart said it reduced Exotel’s cost per minute by up to 57% compared with those services, while cutting response times from 1.1 seconds to under 300 milliseconds.Unlike providers that buy or reserve computing capacity and resell it, Simplismart does not own computing capacity. Instead, it supplies software that enables cloud companies to offer AI services using their graphics processing units (GPUs) without building the software themselves.Yotta is using the offering for Shakti Studio, allowing customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure, the company said.Co-founder and chief technology officer Devansh Ghatak said the funding would also support the development of software to match AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and time zones, helping cloud providers use their existing equipment more efficiently.You use AI every day. articles.body: Bengaluru: Global private equity investor Advent International has raised $30 billion across its funds, including nearly $27 billion for its 11th flagship fund and more than $3 billion for a new mid-market strategy, as it expands its investment capabilities and international presence.Advent International GPE XI raised more than its $26 billion target, while the new Advent Mid-Market Private Equity fund is the firm’s first dedicated vehicle for smaller buyouts and growth investments. articles.title: CEOs bet on growth, resilience and AI: Survey
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: CEOs in India aim to sustain growth amid rising geopolitical uncertainty, with resilience, talent development and the ability to translate AI
articles.body: NEW DELHI: CEOs in India aim to sustain growth amid rising geopolitical uncertainty, with resilience, talent development and the ability to translate AI investments into measurable business gains emerging as key priorities. The challenge lies in capitalising on India’s economic momentum while strengthening cyber security and preparing the workforce for future demands, according to a KPMG survey shared exclusively with TOI.The survey, conducted between Aug and Sept among 1,400 CEOs globally, including 125 in India, found that business leaders remain confident about growth, supported by investment in talent and technology, scenario planning and efforts to build more agile and resilient organisations.``For India’s CEOs, the biggest opportunities lie in the country’s growth momentum, AI-led transformation and sustainable value creation. At the same time, success will depend on how effectively organisations address cybersecurity risks, build future-ready talent and translate technology investments into measurable business outcomes’’, Yezdi Nagporewalla, CEO, KPMG in India said.Notably, 69% of CEOs in India are confident about the global economic outlook, compared with 65% of CEOs worldwide. The same proportion of India’s business leaders expect earnings to grow by 2.5% or more over the next three years, up from 61% in the previous year,However, the growth outlook remains exposed to significant risks. Globally, cyber and data security is the greatest threat to growth, followed by the global economic outlook, geopolitical instability and regulatory pressures. These concerns have contributed to a decline in CEOs’ confidence in the outlook.Further, attracting and retaining employees is the biggest workforce challenge for 54% of India’s CEOs, higher than the global average of 47%, the CEO Outlook study said.Despite these challenges, hiring plans remain strong. As many as 92% of India’s CEOs expect headcount to increase over the next three years, with 34% anticipating growth of 6% or more, compared with 27% of CEOs globally expecting an increase. At the same time, organisations are preparing for AI-related disruption through retraining, recruitment, role redesign and greater attention to skills gaps, the survey said.The survey also highlights a shift. While 2025 was focused on building readiness for an AI-led future, 2026 is about converting that preparation into growth through responsible AI deployment, cyber resilience, and talent transformation.For India, the emphasis on domestic large language models (LLMs) and trusted AI ecosystems adds a further dimension to the AI agenda, reflecting a focus on developing home-grown capabilities.You use AI every day. articles.title: Exclusive-GM plans to offer hybrid SUVs in strategic pivot
articles.summary: By Kalea Hall DETROIT, Oct 27 (Reuters) - General Motors plans to introduce hybrid versions of its popular three-row SUVs, a strategic shift after heavily in...
articles.body:
DETROIT, Oct 27 (Reuters) - General Motors plans to introduce hybrid versions of its popular three-row SUVs, a strategic shift after heavily ‌investing in electric vehicles, according to people familiar with the matter.

The ‌automaker plans to build hybrid models of the Chevrolet Traverse, Buick Enclave and GMC Acadia at ​a factory in Lansing, Michigan, the people said. Combined, those mechanically similar models are among GM's strongest sellers in the US.

The timing of the planned hybrid models couldn't be learned.

GM CEO Mary Barra told analysts during the ‌company's earnings call last week ⁠that the automaker would have hybrids in multiple segments.

"We will have hybrids. They've already been added. It's not going to be ⁠additional (capital expenditures) and engineering," she said. "We'll talk more about them as we get closer to the launch."

US hybrid sales have taken off this year as car shoppers seek ​relief ​from higher gas prices. GM, which only ​sells a hybrid version of the ‌Chevy Corvette in the US, has lost market share this year, while strong hybrid players like Toyota have gained.

GM dealers have complained about the automaker's lack of hybrids, which combine a gas engine with a lithium-ion battery and electric motor to conserve fuel and boost power.

Dealers have been ‌pressing the company to add hybrids to ​its lineup, including during recent regional meetings between ​retailers and GM sales executives, ​according to dealers who have attended.

"We've been telling them every ‌chance we get that we need hybrids," ​one dealer said.

GM ​executives in the past have said that hybrids add too much cost and complexity, and that they preferred to invest in EVs.

articles.title: Premium liquor demand holds up in Sept qtr
articles.summary: Premium liquor demand stayed strong in Sept quarter as Radico, United Breweries and ABD posted higher sales; premium volumes rose despite cost pressures.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Indians continued to spend on pricier beer and spirits in the September quarter, helping liquor makers post stronger sales and profits even as costs remained high.Radico Khaitan reported total income of Rs 5,588 crore for the quarter, up 10% from a year earlier, while net profit rose 66% to Rs 232 crore. The maker of Magic Moments vodka and Rampur whisky saw volumes of its Prestige & Above, or higher-priced, liquor rise 35.8%, while volumes of its regular products fell 9.7%.Premium products now account for 77.1% of Radico’s Indian-made foreign liquor revenue, up from 68.6% a year earlier. Managing director Abhishek Khaitan told **TOI** that the company was increasingly focusing on premium liquor and would sell regular products selectively in states where they remained profitable.Vodka has been a major driver. Khaitan said vodka now accounts for 6.3% of liquor sold in India, compared with 3.7% about two years ago, while Radico controls around 60% of the vodka market. He expects the shift to continue for several years.United Breweries, the maker of Kingfisher beer, reported total income of Rs 4,664 crore, up 24% from Rs 3,752 crore a year earlier. Profit for the quarter nearly tripled to Rs 135 crore from Rs 46 crore.Overall beer volumes rose 16%, but premium beer volumes jumped 38%. Heineken Silver volumes grew 67%, while Kingfisher Ultra volumes rose 44%. Volumes of its Prestige & Above products rose 6.1% to 4.5 million cases, while its lower-priced Mass Premium & Others portfolio grew faster, rising 15.5% to 5.5 million cases. However, revenue from the premium portfolio still rose 13.4%, as the company earned more on every case sold.ABD’s overall quarterly volumes crossed 10 million cases for the first time. Its operating profit margin slipped to 12.4% from 13.1% as spending on brands and its new luxury portfolio, along with a Rs 29-crore hit from global supply-chain disruptions, eroded some of the gains.Karnataka also emerged as a common bright spot. Khaitan said Radico’s premium portfolio in the state grew 120% after liquor duties were rationalised, making higher-priced brands relatively more affordable. articles.title: Air India, IndiGo begin Digi Yatra international trials at seven airports
articles.summary: Air India and IndiGo begin Digi Yatra international passenger trials from Nov 1 at seven airports for Indian e-passport holders, running through December.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Indian passengers flying abroad on Air India and IndiGo will be able to use Digi Yatra at seven airports from Nov 1, as the facial-recognition platform moves from technical tests to passenger trials for international travel.The beta programme is limited to Indian nationals holding e-passports, which contain an embedded electronic chip. It will cover Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports and run through December. Passenger feedback will help shape a wider rollout planned for 2027, Digi Yatra Foundation said.Travellers can use the service at terminal entry points, security hold areas and boarding gates where the necessary infrastructure is available. The trial covers all international destinations served by Air India and select destinations served by IndiGo.**TOI** had first reported in April that Digi Yatra was testing international travel and passport-based enrolment. Those technical trials, conducted with IndiGo on routes including Bengaluru-Doha, tested whether digital identity credentials could work across airports. The latest phase allows eligible passengers to use the service during their journeys.The trial does not replace immigration or airline document checks. Passengers must still carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory formalities.To enrol, passengers need to scan their e-passport using the Digi Yatra app, read its chip with a compatible smartphone’s near-field communication (NFC) feature and take a selfie. Once verified, the digital credential is stored in the Digi Yatra wallet on their phone.“With the start of international passenger trials, we are taking an important step towards extending this experience to eligible Indian nationals travelling internationally,” said Suresh Khadakbhavi, CEO of Digi Yatra Foundation.The foundation said it would also explore compatibility with global aviation identity frameworks to support the use of credentials across borders.It has also redesigned the app, including its consent screen, to make it clearer what information passengers share, with whom and for what purpose.Digi Yatra said it has more than 2.65 crore users and has enabled over 11 crore journeys. articles.title: Apple hit by 'Crackgate' outcry over iPhone Duo screen problems
articles.summary: The debut of Apple's first foldable iPhone has hit an early snag after some users reported broken screens just days after its release, a phenomenon...
articles.body:
The debut of Apple's first foldable iPhone has hit an early snag after some users reported broken screens just days after its release, a phenomenon already dubbed "Crackgate".

The growing furore on social media over the iPhone Duo's apparent problems is a rare setback for a company that stakes much of its reputation on the quality of its hardware.

It is also a blow to Apple's new chief executive John Ternus , who took over from Tim Cook last month. Ternus, who investors have hoped will breathe new life into Apple's product roadmap, is set to hold his first quarterly results call on Monday.

Apple has acknowledged that a "small number" of devices had broken following the Duo's release on Friday.

"We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units," Apple said. "If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement."

Over the past week, several social media posts from around the world have shown iPhone Duos with the same horizontal crack about two-thirds of the way down the screen when the device is open.

While the scale of the problem with the Duo remains unclear, "Crackgate" evokes memories of another iPhone launch misfire.

In 2010, iPhone 4 users reported dropped calls and weak signal in a phenomenon dubbed "Antennagate". After Apple's then-CEO Steve Jobs initially dismissed the complaints as customers "holding it the wrong way", the company later issued free protective bumpers.

Apple has not announced a recall on any of its foldable devices. Such a move would be highly unusual for the company, which has historically used service and replacement programmes to address issues.

This month's launch of the Duo, which costs upwards of $2,000 , marked the biggest design change for the iPhone in its nearly 20-year history. Apple's entry into the foldable phone market came seven years after its main rival Samsung debuted the first Galaxy Fold device.

Several other foldable phones have also faced reliability problems. In 2019, Samsung experienced early issues with what was then new display technology, after some review units experienced screen breaks.

Ternus said Apple had waited to avoid offering a "cheap and crappy" device and instead perfected the complex engineering required to create a smooth internal display and durable hinge.

Francisco Jeronimo, a vice-president at market intelligence firm the International Data Corporation, said the Duo issues showed that "even a company with Apple's engineering resources and supply chain discipline faces a steep learning curve in foldables".

articles.title: White House tempers tough talk on Canada trade as inflation tops voter concerns
articles.summary: Trump’s combative approach to Canada appears to be softening just days before midterm elections where tariff fueled inflation is a primary concern for voters.
articles.body: The Trump administration’s combative approach to Canada appears to be softening slightly, just days before the midterm elections in the U.S., where tariff-fueled inflation is a primary concern for voters. Trade talks with Washington have seen a “slight intensification” in recent days, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Monday. President Donald Trump, likewise, seemed to back off some of his angrier rhetoric over the weekend, when he told reporters a potential trade deal with Canada would be “settled pretty soon.” “They’re willing to give us anything at this moment,” Trump added. Carney, however, said the opposite. “To the extent any progress has been made, it’s because the U.S. is coming closer to our position,” he told reporters in Ottawa. Ever since advanced trade talks collapsed in August, the Trump administration has slapped 50% tariffs on hundreds of categories of Canadian imports. Ottawa has responded in kind. But the two leaders’ most recent statements came after the United States unilaterally announced that it would lift some tariffs on Canada late last week and replace them with others. The move to alter tariffs came at the urging of Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who is facing a tight re-election battle in Maine. Control of the U.S. Senate will be decided Tuesday by a handful of very close races, several of them in Canadian border states where polls show Trump’s tariffs are broadly unpopular. In Alaska, candidates across the political spectrum have called out Trump’s trade war with Canada as a drag on consumers. The same is true in Michigan, where the Republican nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers, has called for an end to the trade war with Canada. The economies in all three of these states are deeply intertwined with their Canadian neighbors. In Washington, a White House official who is not typically involved in trade talks suggested over the weekend that a trade agreement was imminent. The U.S. and Canada are “very close to finally having a deal,” said Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, on Fox News. But neither the American nor the Canadian statements since then appeared to support such a sunny reading of the situation. The Commerce Department, which oversees trade, did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday from NBC News. “Canada remains in constructive dialogue with our U.S. counterparts on a range of priorities,” said a spokesperson for the minister responsible for trade with the United States. Meanwhile, Carney said he didn’t know whether the motivations of American officials hoping to revive talks were different this time. “We have very clear bottom lines, red lines, which meant that we were not willing to sign what was offered in August,” he said Monday.

articles.title: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season

articles.body:
We are only two days into the week, and it already feels like it should be the weekend.

In the past two days, Meta ( META ) said it will raise $95 billion to support its AI build-out through stock offerings, and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) dropped a 407-page IPO prospectus that I know you haven't read in its entirety. (Wall Street hasn't either, so don't lose sleep over it.)

Lost in that activity is that earnings season continues in full swing, with results from Coca-Cola ( KO ), Hilton ( HLT ), UPS ( UPS ), Whirlpool ( WHR ), and others today.

While investors are jacked up about AI and some stability returning to the tech trade, don't lose sight of earnings season: After all, it's earnings and earnings expectations that power stocks, not Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei (although his comments have moved markets in the past).

So here are a few quick takes on a couple of earnings reports I chewed through this morning:

I don't have any problems with this Hilton quarter, even though the stock is getting hit on a slight revenue miss. The important revenue per available room metric grew 5.8%, the company remains an aggressive buyer of its stock, and it approved the development of 30,500 rooms in the quarter.

The report fits nicely with the Delta ( DAL ) report we got last week, in that higher fuel prices don't appear to be slowing leisure or business travelers.

I think it also fits nicely with the numbers out of UPS today, with US sales up 4.5% and its full-year guidance hike.

Coca-Cola's latest guidance lift reinforces the view that the company continues to take massive market share away from rival PepsiCo ( PEP ). Coke Zero sales surged 16%.

Not a good day for the team at PepsiCo up in Purchase, N.Y.

A weak housing market is hurting appliance sales

I continue to be absolutely shocked by what's happening at Whirlpool ( WHR ). Another supersoft quarter, with an adjusted loss of $0.21 per share. Costs are up, and the business is being hurt by a near-frozen US housing market.

You need nerves of steel to buy Whirlpool shares here — the stock is down more than 63% this year. If you do, the thesis has to be that the iconic company is acquired at some point in the next 12 months.

articles.title: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
articles.summary: Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November’s midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll, 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances…
articles.body:
Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November’s midterm elections.

In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite.

Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer.

The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle.

September saw an uptick in annual inflation for Americans, with the cost of energy, gas and electricity rising from August to September.

Democrats have campaigned on targeting the Trump administration’s tariffs and the war in Iran — two factors behind U.S. price hikes. Amid the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the oil industry, has been closed.

According to AAA , the average price of a regular gallon of gas in the U.S. has risen from about $3.05 last year to about $4.27 as of Tuesday afternoon. The average price of a gallon of diesel has risen in the last year, sitting at about $6.35 as of Tuesday afternoon compared to its $3.66 a gallon price in 2025.

In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll, 52 percent of respondents said they would cast their ballot for a Democrat for their congressional district if the election occurred that day, while 42 percent said the same of a Republican.

Two percent backed a third-party candidate while 1 percent were not sure about their election. Three percent of respondents did not provide an answer.

The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll took place from Oct. 19 to 20, featuring 1,289 registered voters and plus or minus 3.7 percentage points as its margin of error.

articles.title: Microsoft and Skydance announced buyouts. What does it mean for workers in a 'low-hire' market?
articles.summary: Microsoft and Skydance announced voluntary buyouts this week to thousands of workers. Here's what to consider if you're one of them.
articles.body:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Skydance ( SKYD ) announced voluntary buyouts this week, cutting payrolls amid underlying business shifts and increased investor scrutiny.

Microsoft announced its largest voluntary buyout ever, offering it to about one-quarter of its staff, or 60,000 people.

Eligible Microsoft employees have until early December to decide whether to accept the voluntary exit offer, with participating workers scheduled to leave by Dec. 31.

Skydance is offering some employees a one-time voluntary buyout, three weeks after Paramount Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery in a $111 billion deal.

"As we bring our ⁠teams together, we recognize that not everyone will ​see their future here, and we respect that," Skydance ​CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said in a memo to employees . It did not specify the number of employees targeted.

Companies use buyouts as a fast way to bolster their bottom line.

Buyouts can motivate employees to leave and avoid mass layoffs, though they can also be an early signal that layoffs are ahead.

In most cases, buyout packages are at least worth considering. If you've been offered one, there's a real possibility that your position has already been targeted for cuts.

In general, if you're part of a company-wide layoff, it's not likely to come with as generous a package. It might be only straight severance pay, often one or two weeks' pay for every year you've been on the payroll.

If you're nearing 65, when Medicare kicks in and full Social Security benefit eligibility is not too far away, you might accept the offer without too much anxiety.

If you've been socking away retirement savings for decades, and your 401(k) or IRA accounts are well-funded, you might be in a position to happily say yes and move on.

If you're in the thick of your working years, the state of the job market and economy when you get your buyout offer shouldn't be ignored.

The current average length of unemployment is 25.4 weeks, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Roughly 3 in 10 of all unemployed individuals have been out of work for nearly half a year or longer.

Would a buyout offer continue paying you if your job search took that long?

This year, unemployment is low, but people are holding onto their jobs, and the labor market has been characterized as low-hire, low-fire.

That doesn't make things easy for those hunting for a job.

"Employees have been emotionally battered by layoffs, AI, resurgent inflation, and more," Glassdoor chief economist Daniel Zhao told Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Google to report Q3 results as investors focus on AI growth, weigh Meta Muse AI risk
articles.summary: Google will report its third-quarter earnings Wednesday.
articles.body:
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) will report its third-quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, as Wall Street braces for a deluge of information about the health of the AI trade.

Investors have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.

Those fears came into focus last week, as traders dumped shares of CoreWeave over questions about its massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.

For the third quarter, analysts anticipate Google will report earnings per share of $3.01 on revenue of $127.8 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs is expected to come in at $111.2 billion.

Google's advertising segment is projected to see sales of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit could see revenue jump 91% to $28.9 billion.

The company could also book significant revenue on the sale of its custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) to third-party data centers. On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.

"Near-term, we think TPU sales-driven upside, a competitive agentic offering, and broader Gemini 4 launch could be catalysts," BofA Global Research analyst Justin Post wrote in an investor note.

According to TD Cowen analyst John Blackledge, Google is expected to generate $9.4 billion in TPU sales in the second half of 2026. That, he wrote, could increase to $62.5 billion in 2027 and 138 billion in 2028.

But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta thanks to its new Muse AI agent . According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.

If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.

articles.title: Why Anthropic's IPO contrasts the 'cult of Elon Musk' at SpaceX and Tesla
articles.summary: Anthropic's IPO will test the founder-focused venture capital model, veteran dealmaker Jim Neeson says.
articles.body:
In the first mega IPO of 2026, SpaceX ( SPCX ) singled out one person in its prospectus as the shot caller: none other than the world's richest person, Elon Musk.

The next big IPO of the year — Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), which could be the largest of all time — is run more by a committee of founders. That's a good thing given its mission and structures, according to veteran dealmaker Jim Neeson.

"I would say having seven founders working together can make it where it's not just like a cult of Elon Musk, right?" the Connor Group founding executive said on Sozzi Unleashed . "You actually have it where you have a consortium of people making decisions, which I actually think can be a good thing."

Anthropic publicly files IPO prospectus, noting strong revenue growth and massive spending

5 unexpected risk factors Anthropic is worried about

Anthropic is losing $80 billion on paper — and just made money where it counts

Neeson noted that Anthropic is a public benefit company with seven founders who collectively own 50.1%.

"You have a board that will be approved by sort of a trust fund. And then you also have a business where it's not just going to be about profits. It's also going to be sort of the social benefit piece that's built into their doctrine," he explained.

Anthropic's founders are CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and president, Daniela Amodei, as well as Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Chris Olah. The consortium left OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) to start Anthropic in January 2021.

The seven co-founders will be issued new Class F common stock as part of the IPO, giving them majority control of the company — something Neeson said investors will have to navigate.

"If you look at Meta, [and] you also look at Google, you had very strong founders," Neeson said. "A lot of times that is the venture capital case. I want founders that can make strong decisions and not be beholden to sort of quarterly type of trends."

"This is going to be a different type of structure out there, and it's going to be tested," he added. "We've never seen it, especially at this scale, especially at these growth rates. So I would say that's one thing analysts and investors are going to be looking very closely at."

The group looks to be managing the financials relatively well.

Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed. The filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, a strong signal of aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.

On an adjusted basis, Anthropic posted $1.62 billion in operating income through the first six months of 2026 compared to a loss of $1.85 billion last year.

Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.

Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

articles.title: Coca-Cola CEO responds to Diet Coke 'fridge cigarette' moniker: Consumers call it what they want
articles.summary: The Diet Coke cravings continue, yet again boosting the company's quarter.
articles.body:
We all know a co-worker who heads to the fridge at 2 p.m. to grab a Diet Coke, or what has come to be called a " fridge cigarette ."

Younger Americans coined the term in 2025 to refer to any cold soft drink people crave, but especially Diet Coke, which has grown in popularity in recent years.

"Consumers call it … the way they want to call it," Coca-Cola ( KO ) CEO Henrique Braun said in response to the viral nickname.

Braun is no stranger to the fandom that surrounds the Diet Coke brand. He took over as CEO of the Coca-Cola Company earlier this year after working there as an intern over thirty years ago.

"Coke, it's one of those brands that continue to recruit the next generation of consumers," Braun added.

"The most important thing to us is that we don't position Diet Coke in that way [as a fridge cigarette]," he said. "What we do is that it's a great-tasting product which connects with the consumer in a very unique way … We've seen that with our engagement with consumers end to end from social media all the way down to transactions."

Diet Coke's popularity continues to boost Coca-Cola's quarterly results . In the third quarter, Braun said both Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Zero volumes grew in the double digits in North America, helping to offset flat overall growth in the US.

Diet Coke is "having its moment," CFO John Murphy told Yahoo Finance in July. He chalked up the brand's success to its taste profile.

"It's not much more complicated than that," he said.
